backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace train_y with log10 of the values (use log10(y + eps) with eps set to a small fraction of the minimum positive value if any y is <= 0). Fit the same RandomForestRegressor on the transformed target and return predictions as-is. Clearance values are right-skewed, so a log scale should make tree splits less dominated by a few large values. Spearman is invariant to monotone transforms of the prediction, so no back-transform is needed.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Replace train_y with its rank-normalized version (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, then mapped through the standard normal inverse CDF) before fitting the RandomForestRegressor. This aligns the regression loss with a rank-based metric like Spearman and removes the influence of outliers on split choice. Return the raw model predictions for the test molecules.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the target

backlog.spec: Replace the bit-vector featurizer with Morgan count fingerprints: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the same radius 2 and 2048 size, so each feature holds how many times an environment occurs in the molecule. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. Count information often helps for properties driven by repeated groups, such as the number of polar or metabolically labile fragments.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Change the fingerprint to radius 3 with fpSize 4096 bits (keep bit fingerprints). Larger radius captures more of the local chemical context around each atom, and the bigger vector reduces hash collisions. Everything else in the script stays the same, including the RandomForest hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Larger Morgan radius and bit length

backlog.spec: Compute the full set of RDKit 2D descriptors with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for every molecule, replace NaN and inf values with 0, and clip each column to the 1st-99th percentile range of the training set. Concatenate these descriptors to the Morgan bit vector before fitting the RandomForest. Physicochemical descriptors such as logP, TPSA and molecular weight are strongly linked to hepatic clearance, so they should add signal the fingerprint lacks.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D descriptors to fingerprints

backlog.spec: Instead of the full descriptor list, append only about 10 physicochemical descriptors to the Morgan bits: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, NumAromaticRings, HeavyAtomCount and NumHeteroatoms. Fit the RandomForest on this combined matrix. A short hand-picked list reduces noise from the many irrelevant descriptors and keeps the feature count manageable.
backlog.title: Small curated descriptor set plus fingerprint

backlog.spec: Add the 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) as extra columns alongside the Morgan bit vector, then fit the same RandomForest. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence that a hashed circular fingerprint sometimes misses, and they are cheap to compute.
backlog.title: MACCS keys combined with Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Build two extra featurizers, rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints with 1024 bits each. Concatenate them with the Morgan bits and fit the RandomForest. Different fingerprint families capture different substructure relationships, so the combined vector gives the trees more complementary views of each molecule.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use the Morgan generator with atom invariants from pharmacophoric feature classes (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an FCFP-type atom invariant generator, radius 2, 2048 bits). Groups atoms by donor, acceptor, aromatic and similar roles instead of element identity, so molecules with similar pharmacophores but different scaffolds look more alike. Keep the RandomForest unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant (FCFP-style) Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Before fitting, remove any fingerprint column that is set in fewer than 2 training molecules or in more than 98 percent of them (computed on the training set only, then applied to the test set). This shrinks the feature matrix and removes bits that give trees little usable split information, which speeds up the RandomForest and can reduce overfitting to rare substructures.
backlog.title: Drop near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with kernel ridge regression using a Tanimoto (MinMax on binary fingerprints) kernel, computed as K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) over Morgan bits. Standardize the target to zero mean and unit variance, choose the ridge alpha by a small grid (for example 0.01, 0.1, 1) using an inner 3-fold split of the training data, then predict the test molecules. Tanimoto similarity is the standard metric for molecular similarity, so this kernel suits the task.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process or kernel ridge

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel on the Morgan bit fingerprints (K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max)). Use C=1 and epsilon=0.1 on a standardized target, with the kernel matrix built from the training molecules and the test-to-train kernel for prediction. SVR with a chemically meaningful kernel is often stronger than a forest on small datasets of around 1000 molecules.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with a kNN regressor on Tanimoto similarity: for each test molecule, take its k=10 most similar training molecules by Morgan Tanimoto similarity and predict the similarity-weighted average of their target values, with weights equal to the similarity raised to the power 3. Use the seed only for tie handling. The method is simple and can be a useful ensemble member because it is local in chemical space.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour regression

backlog.spec: Swap the RandomForest for a LightGBM regressor (objective regression, num_leaves 31, learning_rate 0.03, 600 boosting rounds, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) trained on the same Morgan bits. Gradient boosting often beats bagged trees on fingerprint regression when tuned for shrinkage and subsampling.
backlog.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Train an XGBoost regressor (max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.03, 500 rounds, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_weight 3, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bits concatenated with the RDKit descriptor set after NaN cleanup. XGBoost's second-order updates and column subsampling give a different inductive bias from the RandomForest, which is useful for an ensemble later.
backlog.title: XGBoost regressor on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, iterations 800, learning_rate 0.05, loss RMSE, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the RDKit 2D descriptor table with NaN and inf replaced by 0. CatBoost's ordered boosting is robust on small tabular data, and descriptors give it continuous physicochemical features that fingerprints do not express directly.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor using the same n_estimators, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=1 and n_jobs=-1. Extra-Trees draws split thresholds at random, giving smoother predictions and lower variance on noisy labels. Keep the rest of the script unchanged so the only change is the tree ensemble type.
backlog.title: Extra-Trees instead of Random Forest

backlog.spec: Fit the RandomForest on Morgan bits and a LightGBM regressor on the same features, convert each model's test predictions to ranks within the test set, and return the mean of the two rank vectors. Rank averaging is scale-free, so it does not need calibration and suits Spearman scoring. Use a fixed 50/50 weight.
backlog.title: Ensemble of RandomForest and LightGBM by rank averaging

backlog.spec: Build an inner 4-fold out-of-fold prediction set on the training molecules for three base learners (RandomForest, kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel, and LightGBM). Fit a non-negative linear regression (or Ridge with alpha=1) on those out-of-fold predictions, then refit each base learner on all training data and combine the test predictions with the learned weights. Stacking learns how much to trust each model without hand tuning.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with a ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Set min_samples_leaf to 3 in the RandomForest (keep 300 trees and max_features 0.3). Larger leaves average more training molecules per prediction, reducing variance on noisy measured clearance values and typically helping a Spearman-based score on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Larger leaves for smoother RandomForest

backlog.spec: Set max_features to 'sqrt' (about 45 of 2048 bits) instead of 0.3 in the RandomForest. Fewer candidate features per split decorrelates the trees further, which can help when most fingerprint bits are uninformative. Keep the other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower max_features for the RandomForest

backlog.spec: Raise n_estimators to 1000 and set max_samples to 0.7 in the RandomForest with bootstrap enabled. More trees reduce Monte Carlo variance in the prediction, and subsampling rows adds diversity between trees. Runtime should remain within the job budget at 8 threads, so check the timing before accepting.
backlog.title: Increase number of trees with bootstrap fraction tuning

backlog.spec: Compute a weight for each training molecule as the inverse of the local density of its target value (for example a histogram or kernel density estimate of train_y over 20 bins), normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to the RandomForest fit. This pushes the model to fit the sparse tails of the clearance distribution as well as the dense middle, which can help rank correlation across the whole range.
backlog.title: Sample weighting by target density

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles (computed on the training fold only). The forest then stops chasing a handful of extreme measured values that would otherwise distort the leaf averages. Predictions for test molecules come from the unchanged RandomForest.
backlog.title: Winsorize extreme targets

backlog.spec: Standardize the RDKit 2D descriptors (after NaN cleanup and clipping to training percentiles) and fit a RidgeCV model with alphas logspace from -2 to 3 using 5-fold internal cross-validation on the training data. Return its test predictions. A linear model on physicochemical descriptors is a simple, strongly regularized baseline that may rank molecules differently from the forest, which is useful in an ensemble.
backlog.title: Regularized linear model on descriptors

backlog.spec: Train sklearn MLPRegressor on the Morgan bit vector with hidden layers (256, 64), ReLU activation, Adam with learning_rate_init 1e-3, alpha (L2 penalty) 1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 500, and random_state=seed. Standardize the standardized target to zero mean and unit variance before fitting and invert the scaling on predictions. Neural networks on fingerprints can capture smooth structure-activity trends that trees miss.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprints with weight decay

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM with objective 'huber' (alpha set to the 90th percentile of absolute residuals of the training targets), otherwise with the same parameters as the Morgan-bit LightGBM model. Huber loss reduces the pull of outlying measured values on the gradient updates, which suits noisy clearance assays. Keep the descriptor and fingerprint features unchanged.
backlog.title: Huber loss boosting for outlier robustness

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, hold out 15 percent of the training molecules as an inner validation set (split with the seed), train LightGBM with a large round budget (up to 2000) and early_stopping_rounds 50 on the validation Spearman-compatible L2 loss, then retrain on all training data using the best iteration count found. Automatic round selection avoids hand-tuning and adapts to the dataset size in each fold.
backlog.title: Early-stopped boosting via inner validation

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM on Morgan bits with a learning-rate schedule that starts at 0.1 and decays geometrically to 0.01 over 800 rounds (use the callbacks argument with reset_parameter and a learning_rate list). Larger early steps fit the coarse trend quickly and smaller later steps refine it without overfitting. Keep other parameters fixed.
backlog.title: Learning rate decay schedule for boosting

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, train five RandomForest models with seeds derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4), each with 200 trees, and average their test predictions. Averaging separately seeded forests reduces the seed-dependent part of the prediction, which lowers variance of the final ranking across folds.
backlog.title: Bagged ensemble of models over several seeds

backlog.spec: Since the loss is 1 minus Spearman correlation, train the same XGBRegressor settings but swap the objective to a ranking objective. Use XGBRanker with objective='rank:pairwise' and a single query group containing all training molecules (qid all zeros, relevance labels from train_y, binned into about 10 integer grades by quantile if the ranker requires integer labels). Keep the Morgan + descriptor features unchanged, use random_state=seed, and return the ranker's scores for test_smiles as the predictions. Spearman is invariant to monotone output transforms, so the scores need no rescaling.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking objective for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the existing XGBoost model and Morgan + descriptor features, but pass monotone_constraints to XGBRegressor for the six descriptor columns only. Set +1 for MolLogP and MolWt, and 0 for the rest of the columns, including all 2048 fingerprint bits. The prior is that lipophilicity and size tend to raise hepatocyte clearance, so this removes noisy non-monotone splits on the few strong descriptors. Build the constraint tuple from the feature count so its length matches X exactly.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a small block of count features computed by SMARTS matching, appended to the existing descriptor vector. Count carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, aliphatic amines (primary, secondary, tertiary, not amide or aniline), amidines and guanidines, pyridine-like basic nitrogens, and quaternary nitrogens. Ionization state strongly governs clearance and partitioning, and Morgan bits only encode it indirectly. Use rdkit Chem.MolFromSmarts once at module level and count matches with len(mol.GetSubstructMatches(p)). Keep the XGBoost model unchanged.
backlog.title: Ionization-class SMARTS counts

backlog.spec: Add count features for common sites of oxidative metabolism, appended to the descriptor vector. Use SMARTS for: O-methyl and N-methyl groups, benzylic CH2 and CH3 adjacent to an aromatic ring, unsubstituted aromatic CH positions, tertiary aliphatic carbons, thioethers, and N-dealkylatable amines. Precompile the patterns at module level, count matches per molecule, and append the counts plus the ratio of aromatic CH to total aromatic atoms. Hepatocyte clearance is largely driven by these soft spots, so explicit counts give the trees a direct handle the fingerprint bits cannot. Keep XGBoost unchanged.
backlog.title: CYP metabolic soft-spot counts

backlog.spec: Standardize each SMILES before computing any features. Parse the molecule, keep only the largest covalent fragment with rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or by splitting on '.' and taking the fragment with the most heavy atoms, then neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. If standardization fails or the molecule is None, fall back to the raw SMILES. Apply this identically to train and test molecules inside featurize, so counts and descriptors reflect the parent compound rather than counterions. Leave the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and neutralization before featurization

backlog.spec: Add a block of 3D shape descriptors for each molecule. For each SMILES, add hydrogens, embed one conformer with ETKDG using a fixed randomSeed=seed, optimize it with MMFF if the force field is available, and compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, CalcRadiusOfGyration, and CalcSpherocityIndex. If embedding fails, fill with zeros. Append these eight values to the existing descriptor vector and keep the XGBoost model. Limit this to one conformer per molecule so the job stays well inside the 10-minute cap across 15 fits.
backlog.title: 3D conformer shape descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the single XGBoost fit with a two-stage model. First fit a RidgeCV on standardized descriptors only (the six physchem columns, with the features scaled by StandardScaler fitted on the training fold). Compute the training residuals with cross_val_predict using 5 folds so the base predictions are out of fold. Then fit the existing XGBRegressor on the Morgan + descriptor features to predict the residual. At prediction time, return ridge prediction plus XGBoost residual prediction on the test molecules. This lets a smooth linear trend on lipophilicity and size be handled by the linear part while trees model the remainder.
backlog.title: Two-stage residual boosting over a ridge base

backlog.spec: Build an ensemble inside fit_predict. Group the training molecules by Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles on each molecule). Draw 10 bootstrap samples where whole scaffold groups are drawn with replacement, so every bag contains complete skeletons and duplicated scaffolds are weighted by how often they are drawn. Fit an XGBRegressor with the current settings on each bag, using random_state = seed * 100 + bag index, and return the average of the 10 predictions on test_smiles. Averaging over scaffold-level resamples should reduce variance from the few large scaffold families in the training data.
backlog.title: Scaffold-group bootstrap bagging of XGBoost

backlog.spec: Switch the XGBoost booster from gbtree to dart by passing booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and sample_type='uniform'. Keep n_estimators at 500 and learning_rate close to the current value, but raise learning_rate to about 0.05 since DART needs fewer effective trees. The tree dropout acts as a regularizer against a few trees dominating the prediction. Keep the features, seed, and all other settings the same, and return predictions from the trained model on the featurized test set.
backlog.title: DART booster with dropout on trees

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, tune XGBoost hyperparameters on the training data only, then refit. Sample 6 configurations at random from max_depth in {3,4,5,6,7}, learning_rate in {0.02,0.03,0.05}, subsample in {0.6,0.8,1.0}, colsample_bytree in {0.3,0.5,0.7}, and min_child_weight in {1,3,5}, using a random generator seeded by seed. Score each configuration with a 3-fold GroupKFold split on the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, using Spearman correlation as the criterion. Refit the best configuration on all training molecules and predict test_smiles. Cache the featurized matrix once so the inner loop stays within the time cap.
backlog.title: Small in-fold random search over XGBoost settings

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after featurize, fit a first XGBoost model on the full training matrix with the current settings. Keep only the top 512 columns by gain importance (always keep the six descriptor columns). Refit the same XGBoost on the reduced matrix, using the log10 target and the same seed, and predict on the test matrix reduced to the same columns. Selection uses only training rows, so there is no leakage into the test fold.
backlog.title: Importance-based bit selection before XGBoost

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 3 augmented copies of the training matrix. In each copy, set each Morgan bit to zero independently with probability 0.15 (leave the six descriptor columns untouched), using a numpy RNG seeded from the seed argument. Stack the original and copies with the targets repeated, fit the existing XGBoost on the stacked data, and predict on the unaltered test matrix. This regularizes the model toward robustness to missing substructure bits.
backlog.title: Bit-dropout augmentation of training fingerprints

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit sklearn TruncatedSVD with 32 components on the training Morgan block only (fingerprint columns, not descriptors), then transform both the training and test Morgan blocks. Append the 32 latent columns to the existing feature matrix and fit the current XGBoost on the log10 target. The projection is learned from training rows only and uses the seed argument as random_state.
backlog.title: Appended truncated-SVD latent features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build three feature views: (a) the current Morgan radius-2 plus descriptors, (b) Morgan radius-3 with 1024 bits plus descriptors, and (c) MACCS keys plus descriptors. Train a separate XGBoost on each view with the log10 target and the same hyperparameters and seed. Average the three test predictions with equal weights and return the mean. Each view is a separate model, so the ensemble does not require a single shared feature space.
backlog.title: Multi-view ensemble over fingerprint families

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the log10 targets, then for each training molecule find its k=5 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (Morgan bit vectors, excluding itself). Replace each training label with 0.7 times its own log value plus 0.3 times the mean of its neighbours' log values. Fit the existing XGBoost on the smoothed labels and predict the test molecules as before. This denoises labels across close analogues; compute the similarity matrix once per call with numpy.
backlog.title: Neighbour-based target smoothing of training labels

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the current XGBoost on the training set and predict the test molecules. Append the test molecules to the training set with these predicted log10 values as pseudo-labels, and give them sample_weight 0.3 (training rows keep weight 1). Refit XGBoost on the augmented set with the same seed and return its predictions for the test molecules. This is a transductive step that uses only test SMILES, not test labels.
backlog.title: Pseudo-labelling of unlabelled test molecules

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, cut the log10 training targets into 8 quantile bins using training-set quantiles. Train a LightGBM multiclass classifier (class labels = bin index) on the current feature matrix with num_leaves 15, learning_rate 0.05, 300 rounds, and random_state=seed. For each test molecule, return the expected bin index, the sum over classes of class index times predicted probability, as the score. Because the metric is Spearman, the expected ordinal index is a monotone-friendly output.
backlog.title: Quantile-binned multiclass expected-rank model

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train LightGBM on the log10 target with a fixed-size tree budget of 600 rounds, in four cycles of 150 rounds each. At the start of each cycle, reset the learning rate to 0.1 and decay it with cosine annealing to 0.005 across the cycle, continuing from the previous booster via init_model. Save the prediction for the test set at the end of each cycle, and return the mean of the last three snapshot predictions. The schedule is applied through a learning_rates callback.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble with cyclic learning-rate restarts

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, standardize the descriptor columns with training statistics only and keep the Morgan bits as 0/1. Fit sklearn SGDRegressor with penalty='elasticnet', l1_ratio 0.5, alpha 1e-4, max_iter 2000, tol 1e-4, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, and random_state=seed on the log10 target. Return its test predictions. Because it is a sparse linear model on bits, it is a different inductive bias from the tree models and may suit blending.
backlog.title: Elastic-net linear model on fingerprint bits with SGD

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the current XGBoost predictions on the log10 target for the test molecules. Also compute a similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour prediction: for each test molecule, take the k=10 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules, and average their log10 targets with weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Convert both prediction vectors to ranks within the test set and return 0.7 times the XGBoost rank plus 0.3 times the kNN rank. Rank averaging suits the Spearman-based metric.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged blend of XGBoost and kNN regression

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Morgan bits and RDKit descriptors in featurize, and append a 1024-bit Avalon fingerprint per molecule. Compute it with rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonFP(mol, nBits=1024) and convert it to a numpy array with np.array(list(fp), dtype=np.float32). Keep the XGBoost model and the log10 target unchanged. Skip molecules that fail to parse, as the current code does.
backlog.title: Append Avalon fingerprints to Morgan features

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Morgan bits, descriptors, XGBoost model and log10 target. Append the Extended Reduced Graph fingerprint from rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol), which is a fixed-length float vector of about 315 pharmacophore-distance values. Concatenate it to the feature row. This adds pharmacophore-level information that Morgan bits lack and makes no change to the model or the target.
backlog.title: Append ErG reduced-graph fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep the features and the log10 target transform (y + 1e-6, then log10). Change only the XGBoost objective from the default squared error to reg:absoluteerror, which is a median regressor and is robust to the heavy tails in clearance values. Keep the other hyperparameters unchanged. Since the metric is Spearman, the median-type fit may rank better than the mean fit.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective on the log target

backlog.spec: Train three XGBoost models on the same features, each with a different target: log10(y+1e-6), sqrt(y), and the rank of y scaled to [0,1] using scipy.stats.rankdata. Give each model a different seed derived from the seed argument. For each test set, convert each model's predictions to ranks, then average the three rank vectors and return the result. Averaging ranks is safe because the loss is Spearman.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of three target transforms

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute for each training molecule an out-of-fold feature: the Tanimoto-similarity-weighted mean of the log10 labels of its k=5 most similar training molecules, excluding itself and any molecule in its own inner fold (use a 5-fold KFold split with the seed). For test molecules, compute the same feature using all training molecules. Append this one column to the XGBoost feature matrix for both train and test. Use Morgan bit vectors for the Tanimoto computation, and make it bold: it is a stacking-style neighbour feature rather than a blend.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold similarity-weighted label as a stacked feature

backlog.spec: Train 8 XGBoost models in a loop. For model i, draw a random 40% subset of feature columns using np.random.default_rng(seed*100+i), train an XGBoost on those columns only, and use a different random_state per model. Average the 8 predictions in log10 space and return the average. Keep all other XGBoost settings the same as the current script. This targets the high variance of single trees on scaffold-split data.
backlog.title: Random-subspace bagging of XGBoost

backlog.spec: For each molecule, call rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol), then read each atom's float property '_GasteigerCharge'. Replace NaN and inf values with 0. Compute these 6 features: the maximum charge, the minimum charge, the sum of positive charges, the sum of negative charges, the standard deviation of charges, and the charge on the most polar heteroatom (the minimum over N and O atoms). Append them to the existing feature row. Keep the model and the target transform unchanged.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge summary features

backlog.spec: Keep the features and log10 target. Change only the XGBoost hyperparameters: max_depth=7, colsample_bynode=0.2 (with colsample_bytree=1.0), reg_lambda=10, reg_alpha=0.5, min_child_weight=5, subsample=0.7, learning_rate=0.02, and n_estimators=800. Stronger L1 and L2 penalties and per-node feature sampling reduce overfitting to the training scaffolds. Keep random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Ultra-regularized XGBoost with per-node column sampling

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before fitting, augment the training set: for each training molecule, create one new sample by pairing it with a randomly chosen training molecule (rng from the seed). Use lambda drawn from Beta(0.4, 0.4) for each pair, and form the feature row as lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j and the target as lambda*y_i + (1-lambda)*y_j, with y in log10 space. Concatenate the augmented rows to the originals and fit XGBoost on the doubled set. Predict on the unaugmented test features. This is a bold regularizer aimed at smoothing the decision function between molecules.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation of fingerprint rows

backlog.spec: Fit the current XGBoost model on the log10 target. Use model.apply(X) to get the leaf index for each training and test molecule, giving a matrix of shape (n_samples, n_trees). Build a similarity kernel K(a,b) equal to the fraction of trees where a and b land in the same leaf. Fit kernel ridge regression with alpha=1.0 on the training kernel, using the log10 target minus the training mean, and predict the test set with the test-to-train kernel. Return the average of the XGBoost prediction and this kernel ridge prediction, both on the log10 scale. This is bold: it turns the boosted trees into a learned similarity space and smooths it with a kernel.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process-style blend using a kernel on XGBoost leaf embeddings

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold inner CV on the training molecules using the current XGBoost on log10 targets to get out-of-fold residuals. Drop the 10% of training molecules with the largest absolute residual, then refit the final XGBoost on the remaining 90% with the same settings and predict the test molecules. Keep all other settings unchanged. The seed argument drives the inner split and the model.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit after inner-OOF residual screening

backlog.spec: Append RDKit Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with Generate.Gen2DFingerprint, folded to 512 bits) to the existing Morgan plus descriptor vector. Build them once per molecule inside featurize and leave everything else, including the log10 target and XGBoost settings, unchanged. Skip molecules that fail to parse, as the current code does.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints appended

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for both the training and the test SMILES. Compute inverse document frequency for each bit over the union of training and test molecules, multiply each count by idf, and L2-normalize each row. Feed these weighted features plus the existing descriptors to the same XGBoost on log10 targets. The idf is the only new step and uses only SMILES, not labels.
backlog.title: TF-IDF reweighting of Morgan bits with a transductive vocabulary

backlog.spec: Split the training set at the median molecular weight into a small-molecule group and a large-molecule group. Fit one XGBoost on log10 targets for each group, using the same settings as the current script. At prediction time, route each test molecule to the expert for its side of the median and return that prediction. Use a soft blend near the median, with weights from a logistic function of MW (scale 50 Da), so the boundary is smooth.
backlog.title: Two-expert mixture gated by molecular weight

backlog.spec: Replace depth-wise tree growth with grow_policy='lossguide', max_leaves=31, and max_depth=0 in the XGBRegressor, keeping the log10 target and the other settings. Set min_child_weight to 3 and keep subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.5. Use n_estimators=500 with learning_rate=0.03 as before. This tests whether best-first growth with a fixed leaf budget fits the 970-molecule data better than the depth limit.
backlog.title: Lossguide leaf-wise growth with a leaf cap

backlog.spec: Train the XGBoost model in three stages using xgb_model continuation. Stage 1: fit 150 rounds only on the 50% of training molecules whose log10 targets lie closest to the median, with learning_rate 0.05. Stage 2: continue 150 rounds on the 80% closest to the median. Stage 3: continue 200 rounds on all molecules with learning_rate 0.03. Predict with the final model. The schedule is the only change.
backlog.title: Easy-to-hard staged continuation of boosting

backlog.spec: Implement a minimal message-passing network in numpy only. Atom features are a one-hot of element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, and hydrogen count. Use 3 rounds of neighbour-sum message passing with a shared dense layer and tanh, then sum pooling and a linear readout to the log10 target. Train with Adam (lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4) full-batch for 300 epochs with a fixed seed. Average 5 seeds for the final prediction. Keep the code under about 80 lines.
backlog.title: Small numpy message-passing network on molecular graphs

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule inside fit_predict. Give each molecule a sample weight equal to 1 divided by the square root of the count of molecules sharing its scaffold, normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights to XGBRegressor.fit. This keeps large scaffold families from dominating the trees. Do not change the features, the log10 target, or the hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute the Pearson correlation between the 2048 Morgan bit columns on the training features only. Greedily group bits whose absolute correlation exceeds 0.9, and keep one representative per group (the most frequent bit). Pass the kept bits plus the six descriptors to XGBoost on the log10 target. Fit the bit selection inside fit_predict each time so no test molecules are used.
backlog.title: Correlated-bit clustering to shrink the fingerprint

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, draw the max_depth for each of 7 ensemble members at random from {3,4,5,6,7,8} using a numpy RNG seeded by the seed argument. Train each member on the full training set with its own random_state and the same learning rate and subsampling. Average the predictions on the log10 scale and return them. This adds depth diversity with no extra tuning.
backlog.title: Random-depth XGBoost ensemble across seeds

incumbent.description: Apply a log10 transformation to the target values to normalize the distribution before training.

memo: Helped: swapping random forest for XGBoost (0.6103 to 0.5470) and a log10 target transform (0.5090). These are the only accepted changes; the incumbent is 0.5090. Did not help: ExtraTrees (0.6108), RidgeCV (0.6295), CatBoost on descriptors only (0.7016), Atom-Pair/Torsion fingerprints (0.5266), radius 3 with 4096 bits (0.5251), MACCS (0.5635), bit selection (0.5142), plain LightGBM (0.5791). Within noise (sd about 0.0070): ionization SMARTS (0.5085), 3D descriptors (0.5127), rank target (0.5129), ultra-regularized XGBoost (0.5116). Winsorizing and min_samples_leaf gave exactly 0.5090, so they did nothing. The best near-miss is a 7-model XGBoost ensemble with random depths (0.5052, -0.0038); it is worth a replicate or seed-bagging. Feature additions look exhausted. Many slots were lost to crashes or patch failures, so keep edits small and copy SEARCH text exactly. Next: tune learning rate, tree count and subsample on the log target. Try a rank-averaged XGBoost and LightGBM blend. Replicate close calls.
